result.title: Reading, Not Adapting: Unlocking Frozen Visual Knowledge for AI-Generated Image Detection
result.summary: Generalization to unseen image generators has driven efforts to adapt pretrained visual representations for detection. Yet recent findings show that vision foundation models already encode transferable detection knowledge, while further adaptation can impair generalization. This motivates a shift from backbone adaptation to knowledge readout. Conventional linear probing offers a direct way to read this knowledge but is limited to final-layer RGB features. Multi-cue detectors broaden the evidence base, but their designs introduce other tradeoffs: adaptation may compromise pretrained transferability, heterogeneous encoders complicate feature integration, and late fusion precludes intermediate cross-view interaction. To overcome these limitations, we propose ReMoT, a Mixture-of-Transformers-inspired framework that reads complementary knowledge from spatially aligned RGB and wavelet views within a fully frozen visual foundation. ReMoT employs staged joint attention to enable controlled local and global cross-view interaction, while learnable fusion queries progressively read complementary evidence across Transformer depth without writeback. ReMoT achieves 91.2% average accuracy across eight benchmark groups with 3,074 trainable parameters, attaining the highest overall average among the evaluated methods. These results support structured knowledge readout as a promising alternative to backbone adaptation. Code is available at https://github.com/yunncheng/ReMoT.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 AI 生成图像检测的跨生成器泛化，提出 ReMoT：在完全冻结的视觉基础模型中，通过分阶段联合注意力和可学习 fusion queries 从空间对齐的 RGB 与小波视图跨 Transformer 深度读取互补证据，仅用约 3 千个可训练参数，在八个基准组上平均准确率 91.2%。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「不改写冻结骨干、用可学习 query 分层读取中间层证据」的设计，可能为 LVR 中如何在不扰动视觉表示的前提下筛选并汇聚跨深度视觉证据提供线索；但任务是检测而非推理，该读出方式能否用于构建 latent 状态尚待核查。
